_comment: Project-scoped MCP servers. Both talk to the RUNNING dev server, so start it
first with `iex-server` (devenv script) -- they will show as disconnected until
the endpoint is listening on :4000.
Drift checklist: keep this file and opencode.json in lockstep -- see
scripts/mcp-sync.md.
tidewave: Dashbit's runtime-intelligence server (Apache-2.0, free).
mix.lock holds 0.9.2. Tidewave 0.9.0 (Aug 2026) REMOVED the get_*_schema
family incl. get_ash_resources; project_eval, execute_sql_query, get_docs,
get_source_location and get_logs remain. See docs/research/beam-observer-tooling.md.
ash_ai_dev: the dev-time MCP server that ash_ai itself mounts. Kept because this
repo is a reference for ash_ai and should demonstrate it, but note that
upstream describes it as experimental. Its tool list is fixed in ash_ai today;
`dev_tool_domains:` shipped in ash_ai 1.4.1, so ash_agent_tools' adapter can
join it. The adapter is still mounted separately at /ash_agent/mcp (router.ex,
dev only) -- an in-app alternative to the ash-agent daemon below, with the
same tool names. Not registered here, to avoid duplicate tools.
ash_agent (DX-2): the ash_agent_tools dev-only dependency IS an MCP
server -- the read-only introspection surface (describe/validate/
search/context/forbidden/status/reload) over MCP-over-Plug. Boot it
separately with `mix ash_agent.serve --port 4197` from the repo root
(compile-only; it must NOT share the iex-server VM), loopback :4197,
no auth (POST-only; verified 2026-10-09 -- the old :4100 target is
squatted on this host by a WorkOS-emulate container, which is where
the mystery 401s came from). Shows as disconnected until a daemon is
listening. Pre-launch gate:
eval/trigger_eval/ in the package (75% per tool; green 2026-09-21).
ollaya (optional, advisory, local-only): the in-zone decision runtime's own MCP
server, started over stdio as `ollaya mcp` (the binary is `ollaya`). Needs the
`ollaya` binary on PATH; without it the entry shows as disconnected, which is
fine. The endpoint comes from the environment (OLLAYA_BASE_URL, OLLAYA_API_KEY,
the names config/runtime.exs reads); nothing is hardcoded here. Never run it on
the shared platform host: point it at an in-zone endpoint (ADR 0042, ADR 0045).
Serena (optional, not configured here): if installed, point its Elixir backend
at our Expert fork via ls_specific_settings.elixir.ls_path -- see
docs/research/serena-semantic-edits.md. Two-server shape lands with CAP-3.
The PRODUCTION MCP server is a different thing entirely -- it exposes this
application's Ash actions as tools to external agents over OAuth 2.1, and is
mounted in the router, not here.
